record.title: Problems Around Polynomials — Conjecture 7
record.statement: [J. Forsg\aa rd, V. Kostov, B. Sh, hopefully good, see ] For an arbitrary sign pattern $\sigma$, the only type of pairs $(pos,neg)$ which can be non-realizable has either $pos$ or $neg$ vanishing. In other words, for any sign pattern $\sigma$, each pair $(pos,neg)$ satisfying [source label: stand] with positive $pos$ and $neg$ is realizable.
record.source_name: Shapiro - Problems Around Polynomials: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly (2015)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.3
record.statement: If $f(z)$ is meromorphic of finite order $\rho$ and $\sum\delta(a,f)=2$, it is conjectured that $\rho=n/2$, where $n$ is an integer and $n\geq 2$, and all the deficiencies are rational. F. Nevanlinna has proved this result on the condition that $f(z)$ has no multiple values, so that $n(r,a)=\overline{n}(r,a)$ for every $a$ (see also R. Nevanlinna ).
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 1.11
record.statement: If $f(z)$ is a meromorphic function of finite order with at least one finite deficient value, does the conclusion of Problem 1.10 hold?
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 2.17
record.statement: If $f(z)$ is a non-constant entire function and \[b(r)=\left(r\frac{d}{dr}\right)^2\log M(r,f),\] then $$ \limsup_{r\to\infty} b(r)\geq A $$ where $A$ is an absolute constant, such that $0.18<A\leq\frac{1}{4}$, see Hayman . What is the best value of $A$? It seems fair to conjecture that the correct constant in ([source label: 2.3]) is in fact $\frac{1}{4}$.
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 2.24
record.statement: Can an entire function have all its zeros and ones on two distinct straight lines, having infinitely many on each line? Edrei has proved (unpublished) that if $l, m$ are intersecting straight lines, then it is impossible for all the zeros of an entire function $f(z)$ to lie on $l$, and all the ones on $m$. (A. Edrei)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 2.77
record.statement: Let $\Omega$ be a component of the normal set of an entire function $f$ (under iteration). Do there exist such an $f$ and such an $\Omega$ with the following properties: [(a)] ; $f^n(\Omega)$ is uniformly bounded, for $n = 0,1,2,\ldots$; ; $f^n(\Omega)\cap f^m(\Omega)=\emptyset$ for $n\neq m$. (I. N. Baker, R. Herman and I. Kra; communicated by D. Hamilton)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 3.7
record.statement: Problem 1.17 can be reformulated for subharmonic functions, if we replace $\log M(r,f)$ by a general subharmonic function $u(z)$. The same positive theorems hold, and the same conclusions are conjectured in the general case.
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.7
record.statement: Let $f(z)=z^n+a_1z^{n-1}+\ldots+a_n$ be a polynomial of degree $n$. Cartan proved that the set $|f(z)|\leq1$, which we call $E^{(n)}_f$ can always be covered by discs, the sum of whose radii is at most $2e$. It seems likely that $2e$ can be replaced by $2$. If $E^{(n)}_f$ is connected, this was proved by Pommerenke , who also proved the general result, with $2.59$ instead of $2$.
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 4.16
record.statement: Is it true that for all but $o(2^n)$ polynomials $P(z)$ \[\min_{|z|=1}|P(z)|<1,\] or, if not, what is the corresponding correct result?
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.14
record.statement: $f'-f^n\neq a$, where $a$ is some complex number, and $n\geq 5$ if $f$ is meromorphic, $n\geq3$ if $f$ is entire. The corresponding results for functions in the place are proved by Hayman , except for the case $n=1$ of Problem 5.12, which is a result of Clunie .
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.32
record.statement: Suppose that $f_n\in\mathcal{B}_S$. What does $\|f_n-f\|_\mathcal{B}\to0$ as $n\to\infty$ mean geometrically for the functions $g_n$ related to $f_n$ by ([source label: B5.11])? (Ch. Pommerenke)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.66
record.statement: Let $B$ be an infinite Blaschke product in $\mathbb{D}$. Does there exist a positive $\delta$, depending on $B$, such that, for every $w$, $|w|<\delta$, the set $B^{-1}(\{w\})$ is infinite? Stephenson has obtained some related results. (K. Stephenson)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.71
record.statement: Suppose that \[f(z) = \sum^\infty_{k=1}a_kz^{n_k}, \hspace{1cm}n_{k+1}/n_k\geq q>1,\] is an analytic function in $\mathbb{D}$ with Hadamard gaps, such that $T(r,f)\to\infty$ as $r\to1$. Does $\delta(w,f)=0$ hold for every (finite) complex number $w$? (T. Murai)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 5.74
record.statement: Characterise those non-negative measurable functions $f$ on the unit circle that are dominated almost everywhere by moduli of the boundary values of an analytic function in the unit disc with positive real part. (Problem 5.73 might be considered a step towards solving this problem.) (B. Korenblum)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.2
record.statement: Define $A_n=\sup_{f\in S}|a_n|$. It is shown by Hayman that \[\frac{A_n}{n}\to K_0,\hspace{1cm}\text{ as }n\to\infty.\] Is it true that $K_0=1$? The best known result so far is $K_0<1.243$ due to Milin .
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.6
record.statement: What are the orders of magnitude of the $c_n$ in Problem 6.4? Springer obtained the estimate \[|c_n|\leq\frac{2^n}{n}\] and also showed that, given $\varepsilon>0$, \[|c_{2n-1}|>(1-\varepsilon)2^{2n-2}e/(\pi n^3)^{\frac{1}{2}}\] is possible for all sufficiently large $n$.
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.16
record.statement: Let $S^*$ be the class of all star-like functions $f(z)$ in $S$. Marx conjectured that for each fixed $z_0$, $|z_0|<1$, the set of all numbers $f'(z_0)$ for $f\in S^*$ coincides with the set of all number $k'(z)$, $|z|\leq |z_0|$, where \[k(z)=\frac{z}{(1-z)^2}\] is the Koebe function. This is known to be true for $|z|\leq 0.736$, see Duren . (P. L. Duren)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.33
record.statement: The same questions as in Problem 6.32 can be asked under the alternative hypothesis that $\mathbb{C}\setminus\{f(\mathbb{D})\}$ is a single piecewise analytic slit from some finite point ($\omega_0$, say) to $\infty$ lying in an infinite sector with opening $\alpha\pi$ $(0<\alpha\leq2)$ and vertex $\omega_0$. (K. W. Lucas and D. A. Brannan)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.36
record.statement: Suppose that $f$ in $S$ and define \[f_p(z)=[f(z)]^p=z^p+\sum^\infty_{n=p+1}a_{n, p}z^n.\] What can be said about bounds for $a_{n,p}$? If $|a_{n,1}|\leq Kn$ for all $n$ and fixed $K$, then, for integral $p$, \[|a_{n,\,p}|\leq K^p\frac{2p(2p+1)\ldots(n+p-1)}{(n-p)!},\] but it might be easier to obtain bounds for $f_p$ than for $f$. (W. K. Hayman)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.38
record.statement: With the notation of Problem 6.37, is it true that \[\sum^\infty_{n=1}n^{-\beta}d_n^2<\infty\] where $\beta=(\sqrt{2}-1)^2$? (K. W. Lucas)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.43
record.statement: Using the notation of Problem 6.42, it is well-known that \[\Big|\sum^\infty_{k=1}k\gamma_kz^k\Big|=O\Big(\frac{1}{1-r}\Big),\hspace{1cm}r\to1-,\] for $|z| = r < 1$; is it true that \[\sum^\infty_{k=1}k|\gamma_k|r^k=O\Big(\frac{1}{1-r}\Big),\hspace{1cm}r\to1-\,?\] (D. Aharonov)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.49
record.statement: What are the extreme points of the following classes of functions? [(a)] ; Basilevi\^c functions (see Problem 6.48). ; $S^*(\alpha)$ (see Problem 6.48). ; Close-to-convex functions of order $\alpha$, $0 < \alpha < 1$. ; Functions of boundary rotation $k\pi$, $2 < k < 4$. (D. A. Brannan)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 6.83
record.statement: Let $S$ be the usual class of normalised univalent functions in the unit disc $\mathbb{D}$. Characterise those sequences $\{z_n\}$ of points in $\mathbb{D}$ for which $f(z_n) = g(z_n)$ for two different functions $f, g$ in $S$. Notice that a necessary condition is that $\sum^\infty_{n=1}(1-|z_n|) < \infty$, because $(f-g)\in H^p$ for all $p <\frac{1}{2}$. (P. L. Duren)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.4
record.statement: If $z_1=1$, and the $z_i$ are arbitrary complex numbers for $2\leq i\leq n$, then Atkinson proved that \[\max_{1\leq k\leq n}|S_k|>c\] with $c=\frac{1}{3}$. What is the best value for the constant $c$?
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.21
record.statement: Suppose that $|z_k | = 1$ $(1 \leq k < \infty)$. Put \[A_l=\limsup_{m\to\infty}\big|\sum^m_{k=1}z_k^l\big|.\] It is easy to see that there is a sequence $z_k,$ for which $A_l<cl$ for all $l$, and Clunie proved $A_l>cl^{\frac{1}{2}}$ for infinitely many $l$. Is there a sequence for which $A_l = o(l)$ as $l\to\infty$? (P. Erd\"os)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.28
record.statement: Suppose that $f(z)$ is continuous in a domain $D$ and that either [(i)] ; $\int_{|\zeta-z|=r}f(\zeta)\,d\zeta=0$ for all $z\in D$ and $0<r\leq r(z)$, or (weaker), [(ii)] ; $\lim_{r\to0}\Big[r^{-2}\int_{|\zeta-z|=r}f(\zeta)\,d\zeta\Big]=0$ for all $z\in D.$ Does it follow that $f(z)$ is analytic in $D$? (see e.g. , ). (D. Gaier and L. Zalcman)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.46
record.statement: (A `Universal' Phr\'agmen-Lindel\"of Theorem) Let $D$ be an arbitrary unbounded plane domain. Suppose that $f(z)$ is analytic on $D$ and continuous on $\overline{D}$. If $|f(z)|\leq1$ on $\partial D$ and $f(z)=o(|z|)$ at $\infty$, show that $|f(z)|\leq1$ throughout $D$. The $o(|z|)$ would then be the `right' condition since that is what is needed for the case $D=\{z:|z|>1\}$. (D. J. Newman)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.54
record.statement: Let $\phi_t(z)= e^{tz}-1$, $\phi^1_t=\phi_t$ and $\phi^{n+1}_t=\phi_t\circ\phi^n_t$ for $n\geq1$; it follows that \[\phi^1_t(-1)=e^{-t}-1 = -t+\frac{t}{2!}-\ldots,\] \[\phi^2_t(-1)=e^{t(e^{-t}-1)}-1 = -t^2+\ldots\text{ etc.}\] Are the coefficients in these formal power series for $\{\phi^n_t(-1)\}^\infty_{n=1}$ uniformly bounded by $1$ in modulus? (P. J. Rippon)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 7.68
record.statement: For a Hadamard gap sequence $\{n_k\}^\infty_{k=1}$, $n_{k+1}/n_k\geq q>1$, is it true that the measure in $[0,2\pi[$ of the set of those points $x$ for which \[\liminf_{m\to\infty}\Big|\sum^m_{k=1}\cos(n_kx)-\xi\Big|=0,\hspace{1cm}\text{ for all }\xi\in\mathbb{R},\] equals $2\pi$? (T. Murai)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Research Problems in Function Theory — Problem 8.8
record.statement: Suppose that $F$ is a relatively-closed subset of $\mathbb{D}$, and let \[\|f\|_F=\sup\{|f(z)|;z\in F\}\] for functions $f$ in the Bergman space $A^2$. Describe geometrically the set \[\{z: |z|< 1, |f(z)|\leq\|f\|_F\text{ for all }f\in A^2\}.\] (A. Stray)
record.source_name: Hayman - Research Problems in Function Theory (2018)

record.title: Capacitated packing of k-arborescences
record.statement: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph with arc-capacities $c : A \to \mathbb{N}$ and a root node $r_0\in V$. A k-arborescence is the arc-disjoint union of k spanning arborescences rooted at $r_0$. Is it true that if $c(a)\leq l$ for every $a \in A$ and there is a capacity-obeying packing of kl spanning arborescences, then there is a capacity-obeying packing of l k-arborescences?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Disjoint spanning in- and out-arborescences
record.statement: Does there exist a value k so that in every k-arc-connected directed graph D=(V,A) and for every node $v\in V$, there is a spanning in-arborescence and a disjoint spanning out-arborescence rooted in v?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Edge-independent spanning trees
record.statement: In a graph G=(V,E) with a root node r, two spanning trees $T_1$ and $T_2$ are called edge-independent if for any node x in V-r, the unique paths between r and x in $T_1$ and $T_2$ are edge-disjoint. Is it true that if G is k-edge-connected then there exist k edge-independent spanning trees for arbitrary r?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Independent trees
record.statement: In a graph G=(V,E) with a root node r, two spanning trees $T_1$ and $T_2$ are called r-independent if for any node x in V-r, the unique paths between r and x in $T_1$ and $T_2$ are internally node disjoint. Is it true that if G is k-connected then there exist k r-independent trees for arbitrary r?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Orientation of nonideal clutters
record.statement: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a clutter on ground set V, and let $\mathcal{B}$ be its blocker. Is it true that $\mathcal{C}$ is nonideal if and only if there exist $p:{\mathcal C} \to V$ and $q: {\mathcal B} \to V$ such that $p(X)\in X$ for every $X \in {\mathcal C}$, $p(Y)\in Y$ for every $Y \in {\mathcal B}$, if $p(X)=q(Y)$, then $|X \cap Y|>1$?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Partitioning a bipartite graph into proportional factors
record.statement: Let G=(V,E) be a bipartite graph, and $c_1,\dots c_k$ positive reals whose sum is 1. Can E always be partitioned into k parts $E_1,\dots,E_k,$ so that for every $v \in V$ and every $i \in \{1,\dots,k\}$ we have $\lfloor c_i d_E(v) \rfloor \leq d_{E_i}(v) \leq \lceil c_i d_E(v) \rceil$?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Recognition of Seymour graphs
record.statement: A graph G is said to be a Seymour graph if for any edge set F that satisfies $|C\cap F|\le |C\setminus F|$ for every circuit C of G, there exist $|F|$ pairwise disjoint cuts each containing exactly one element of F. Can we decide in polynomial time whether a graph is Seymour?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: Upper bound on common independent set cover
record.statement: For a loopless matroid $M=(S,r)$, let $\Delta(M)=\max_{X\subseteq S} |X|/r(X)$. Let $M_1=(S,r_1)$ and $M_2=(S,r_2)$ be two arbitrary loopless matroids on S. Is it true that S can be partitioned into $\lceil\max\{\Delta(M_1),\Delta(M_2)\}\rceil+1$ common independent sets?
record.source_name: Egres Open - List of open problems

record.title: How many congruent regular tetrahedra can touch at a point
record.statement: How many congruent regular tetrahedra can touch at a point? Easy to show it's at least 20, and at most 22. Apparently, this has been open a long time.

record.statement: Erdős: Show that every (1/2+ľ)|E(ő_(n))| edges of the n-cube ő_(n) contains a C_(4) when n is sufficiently large. (The best known value of ľ is around .19 due to Chung.)
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős)

record.title: Given two permutations σ and τ, what is the expected number of copies of σ in a permutation chosen uniformly at random f
record.statement: : Given two permutations σ and τ, what is the expected number of copies of σ in a permutation chosen uniformly at random from those permutations on n symbols which avoid τ? Newsflash! Miklós Bóna has a nice paper addressing this.

record.title: "1/3 - 2/3 Conjecture" For every poset that is not a chain, there is some pair of elements x and y so that x appears abo
record.statement: Kislitsyn: "1/3 - 2/3 Conjecture" For every poset that is not a chain, there is some pair of elements x and y so that x appears above y in a random linear extension of the poset at least 1/3 of the time and at most 2/3 of the time. See this.

record.title: Are the positive integer powers of 3/2 mod 1 uniformly distributed in the unit interval
record.statement: Are the positive integer powers of 3/2 mod 1 uniformly distributed in the unit interval? One would think so, but apparently this is a hard question. See this.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot)

record.title: Show that there exists a B so that, for every n > 0, there exists a k relatively prime to n whose continued fraction has
record.statement: Niederreiter: Show that there exists a B so that, for every n > 0, there exists a k relatively prime to n whose continued fraction has partial quotients all bounded in average by B. (The sequence a, b, c, d is bounded in average by B if a <= B, a+b <= 2B, a+b+c <= 3B, etc.) Is B=3 already sufficient? If such a B exists, it means that there are "good multipliers" for quasirandom permutations.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Niederreiter)

record.title: Suppose that S is a set of positive integers with the property that S+S -- that is, all sums of the form s_(1)+s_(2) for
record.statement: Erdős-Turán: Suppose that S is a set of positive integers with the property that S+S -- that is, all sums of the form s_(1)+s_(2) for s_(1), s_(2) in S -- contains all sufficiently large integers. (Then S is called an "additive basis".) Is it possible for the number of representations of n as one of these sums to be bounded, for all n? (Conjectural answer: of course not!)
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős-Turán)

record.title: Suppose that S is a set of positive integers with the property that no element is the sum of a nonempty set of other ele
record.statement: Erdős: Suppose that S is a set of positive integers with the property that no element is the sum of a nonempty set of other elements. Such a set is called "sum-free." Let R(S) be the sum of the reciprocals of S. How large can R(S) be? Denote by R the supremum of R(S) over all sum-free S. It is known that R is less than 4, and R > 2.064 (Abbott and Levine-O'Sullivan, respectively).
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Erdős)

record.title: Is it possible to choose 2n points in an n by n grid in the plane so that no three are collinear
record.statement: Dudeney: Is it possible to choose 2n points in an n by n grid in the plane so that no three are collinear? Conjecture: no. In fact, it is conjectured that the answer is still "no" unless 2 is changed to something less than Ŕ/3 = 1.813799.... However, this problem dates back to 1917 and little is known about it. See this.
record.source_name: Cooper - Combinatorial Problems I Like (2020 snapshot) (proposed by Dudeney)

record.statement: Rado: Is it true that, for every n, there is an integer M(n), so that whenever a linear homogeneous equation in n variables is Ramsey (in the positive integers) for M(n)-colors, it is Ramsey for any number of colors?

record.title: How quickly do the gaps between successive primes grow
record.statement: How quickly do the gaps between successive primes grow? Is it slower than n^(ľ) for every ľ > 0? See this.
